questions.title: Why is this not an accordion?
questions.bodytext: A conversation split into closed rows cannot be read straight through or printed. Readers expect to read an interview from start to finish.

questions.title: How is a pair marked up?
questions.bodytext: Each question and answer form one article. The question is a level-three heading and the answer is rich text, so each answer sits under its own question.

questions.title: Why is the question in the accent colour?
questions.bodytext: So readers can spot questions when skimming, without a quotation mark or a "Q:" that a screen reader would read out. The heading level carries the structure; the colour only helps the eye.

questions.title: What does the width field do?
questions.bodytext: It sets the width of the band, not the line length. The text stays at a comfortable reading width, whatever space it has.
